subject: Regulatory evidence request: archival snapshot & LLM data-handling proof
messages:
From: David R. Lowe <david.lowe@umbrabank.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.example, laura_bennett@redwood.example
Cc: compliance@umbrabank.com
Date: 2027-10-30T09:14:00+00:00
Subject: Regulatory snapshot request: short notice evidence for LLM handling of customer data

Karthik / Laura,

We’ve received a regulator notice requesting demonstrable evidence of how Redwood handles customer-provided prompts and whether any of Umbra Bank’s data could have been used to train or improve models. They’ve asked for an archival snapshot covering the last 12 months covering the following:

- A written statement on whether customer prompts/responses are used for model training (and, if so, the opt-out mechanism and logs proving opt-out was respected)
- Retention policy for prompts, responses, KV cache and any derived artifacts (exact retention periods and lifecycle rules)
- A sample extract of audit logs that show prompt ingestion, model selection, and storage events (pseudonymized is fine)
- Any SOC2/SIG/CAIQ artifacts relevant to logging/retention and the specific controls for AI/LLM data handling

We appreciate that some items may be sensitive—Umbra’s compliance team will accept pseudonymized logs and redacted diagrams, but they need enough detail to satisfy an inspection. We need this package within 7 business days.

Can you confirm you can provide an attestation and the listed artifacts and any suggested language for the regulator? If there are any blockers (e.g., data that cannot be exported), be explicit about scope.

Thanks,
David
David R. Lowe
Head of Compliance, Umbra Bank

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.example
To: David R. Lowe <david.lowe@umbrabank.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.example, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example
Date: 2027-10-30T11:02:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Regulatory snapshot request: short notice evidence for LLM handling of customer data

David — thanks for the heads up. We can support; propose the following immediate plan: 

1) Quick attestation draft (legal-reviewed) stating: "Redwood does not use customer data from Umbra Bank for model training unless Umbra opts in via a signed agreement; by default customer prompts and responses are processed for inference only and are retained according to agreed retention policy."

2) Evidence package: 
   - retention table (prompts: 30 days default, ephemeral caches: 0-1 day depending on workload, KV cache stashes: 72 hours by default; per-account overrides possible)
   - pseudonymized log extract showing request_id, model_variant, timestamp, retention_flag
   - infrastructure diagram (storage buckets, lifecycle rules, encryption/KMS)

3) Technical note explaining differences between Hosted API vs Dedicated/Private: Dedicated/Private customers can configure on-prem retention and opt-out enforcement; Hosted customers use account-level flags we honor in our pipeline.

I’ll assemble the attestation + retention_policy_v3.pdf and include the pseudonymized sample logs. Laura, Stephanie — can you prepare the KV cache diagram and the no_train_evidence.csv extract and confirm the exact retention timers we should publish? I’ll also include the SOC2 control references we keep in the evidence folder.

If Umbra needs a notarized/signed attestation we can route through our legal team and DocuSign — I’ll flag that in the follow-up. Target delivery: 2027-11-04 (within seven business days).

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

>
> We’ve received a regulator notice requesting demonstrable evidence of how Redwood handles customer-provided prompts...

From: laura_bennett@redwood.example
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.example
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example, David R. Lowe <david.lowe@umbrabank.com>
Date: 2027-10-31T08:22:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Regulatory snapshot request: archival snapshot & LLM data-handling proof

Karthik / team — attaching the initial artifacts we discussed. Notes below: 

Attachments in this email: retention_policy_v3.pdf, kv_cache_retention_diagram.png, no_train_evidence.csv, s3_audit_snapshot_20271029.txt

Key technical points for the attestation and regulator: 
- Training: Redwood’s default Hosted service does not include customer prompt/response data in downstream model training pipelines. We maintain a clear data flow separation. Training pipelines pull from a dedicated, curated corpus that is explicitly labeled and gated via a change-control process.

- Opt-out enforcement: Customers can set a per-account flag (customer_data_no_train=true). When set, ingestion services mark incoming request records and downstream processors skip any enrichment feeds that would otherwise route data into training corpora. The flag is enforced at the API gateway and persisted in our config store; the audit trail is visible in the provided s3_audit_snapshot_20271029.txt (events: FLAG_SET, INGEST_SHADOW, MODEL_INVOKE).

- Retention specifics (published values):
   - Prompt/response blobs (hosted): 30 days default, configurable to 0 days for Private deployments.
   - KV cache (inference state): ephemeral, default max TTL 72 hours; persisted only for active sessions, truncated per lifecycle policy.
   - Derived telemetry (metrics, aggregates): retained 365 days for product/ops analytics; no PII stored in aggregated telemetry.

- Pseudonymization: sample log rows in no_train_evidence.csv have unique request_hash values rather than raw IDs. We can produce additional pseudonymization if regulator requires stronger guarantees.

Open questions for Umbra: 
- Do you require per-record deletion confirmations (DPA deletion receipts) or is a bulk archival manifest acceptable?
- For SOC2/SIG artifacts: do you want the control mappings (e.g., CC6.1 logging) included inline in the package?

I’ll finalize the attestation text once we confirm those scopes.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Sr. Product Security Manager, Redwood Inference

On Wed, Oct 30, 2027 at 11:02, karthik_iyer@redwood.example wrote:
> David — thanks for the heads up. We can support; propose the following immediate plan...

From: David R. Lowe <david.lowe@umbrabank.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.example, karthik_iyer@redwood.example
Cc: compliance@umbrabank.com
Date: 2027-11-02T16:03:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Regulatory snapshot request: archival snapshot & LLM data-handling proof

Thanks — received and appreciated. A few follow-ups from Umbra compliance: 

- The regulator wants a signed attestation. Please send the final attestation text as a DocuSign link and a PDF.
- For logs: the pseudonymized sample is fine, but we also need a short description of the pseudonymization method (hashing algorithm and whether salts are used).
- SCCs/DPA: please include your standard SCCs mapping for cross-border subprocessors. Umbra will mark which controls are in-scope.

If you can deliver the DocuSign attestation and the augmented pseudonymization description by EOD 2027-11-04 we’ll accept that as meeting the regulator’s timeline. If anything requires more time, flag specific items and estimated dates.

I’ll route the package internally once we have the signed attestation and the extra pseudonymization note. Thanks again for the quick turnaround.

Best,
David
